sanskrit: tato gatajvaro rājā naiṣadhaḥ paravīrahā saṃpranaṣṭe kalau rājan saṃkhyāyātha phalāny uta
english: Then the king of Niṣadha, destroyer of enemy heroes, fever gone, O king — when Kali had wholly vanished — counted the fruits.

sanskrit: mudā paramayā yuktas tejasā ca pareṇa ha ratham āruhya tejasvī prayayau javanair hayaiḥ bibhītakaś cāpraśastaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ kalisaṃśrayāt
english: Filled with supreme joy and blazing with surpassing splendour, the radiant king mounted his chariot and set off with swift horses; the vibhītaka tree, once inauspicious, was now redeemed of its connection with Kali.

sanskrit: hayottamān utpatato dvijān iva punaḥ punaḥ nalaḥ saṃcodayām āsa prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā
english: With a heart overflowing with delight, Nala urged on the excellent horses again and again as they sprang forward like flying birds.

sanskrit: vidarbhābhimukho rājā prayayau sa mahāmanāḥ nale tu samatikrānte kalir apy agamad gṛhān
english: The great-souled king set forth toward Vidarbha; and as Nala passed on, Kali too went home.

sanskrit: tato gatajvaro rājā nalo 'bhūt pṛthivīpate vimuktaḥ kalinā rājan rūpamātraviyojitaḥ
english: Then, O lord of earth, king Nala became free of fever, O king — released by Kali, though still deprived of his own form alone.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca tato vidarbhān saṃprāptaṃ sāyāhne satyavikramam ṛtuparṇaṃ janā rājñe bhīmāya pratyavedayan
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Then, toward evening, the people reported to king Bhīma the arrival of Ṛtuparṇa, a man of true valour, in Vidarbha.

sanskrit: sa bhīmavacanād rājā kuṇḍinaṃ prāviśat puram nādayan rathaghoṣeṇa sarvāḥ sopadiśo daśa
english: At Bhīma's word, the king entered the city of Kuṇḍina, making all ten directions resound with the thunder of his chariot.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ rathanirghoṣaṃ nalāśvās tatra śuśruvuḥ śrutvā ca samahṛṣyanta pureva nalasaṃnidhau
english: Then Nala's horses there heard that chariot-roar; and having heard it, they rejoiced just as they used to in Nala's presence of old.

sanskrit: damayantī ca śuśrāva rathaghoṣaṃ nalasya tam yathā meghasya nadato gambhīraṃ jaladāgame
english: And Damayantī too heard that chariot-sound of Nala — deep as the roar of a cloud at the coming of the rains.

sanskrit: nalena saṃgṛhīteṣu pureva nalavājiṣu sadṛśaṃ rathanirghoṣaṃ mene bhaimī tathā hayāḥ
english: The daughter of Bhīma deemed the chariot-roar exactly like the sound when Nala had held the reins of Nala's own horses of old; and so too did those very horses.

sanskrit: prāsādasthāś ca śikhinaḥ śālāsthāś caiva vāraṇāḥ hayāś ca śuśruvus tatra rathaghoṣaṃ mahīpateḥ
english: The peacocks on the terraces, the elephants in their stalls, and the horses there all heard the chariot-roar of the king.

sanskrit: te śrutvā rathanirghoṣaṃ vāraṇāḥ śikhinas tathā praṇedur unmukhā rājan meghodayam ivekṣya ha
english: Hearing that chariot-roar, the elephants and peacocks likewise cried out with uplifted heads, O king, as if beholding the rise of storm-clouds.

sanskrit: damayanty uvāca yathāsau rathanirghoṣaḥ pūrayann iva medinīm mama hlādayate ceto nala eṣa mahīpatiḥ
english: Damayantī said: As that chariot-roar fills the earth as it were, it gladdens my heart — this must be Nala, lord of the land.

sanskrit: adya candrābhavaktraṃ taṃ na paśyāmi nalaṃ yadi asaṃkhyeyaguṇaṃ vīraṃ vinaśiṣyāmy asaṃśayam
english: If I do not today behold Nala of moon-like face, that hero of numberless virtues, I shall surely perish — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yadi vai tasya vīrasya bāhvor nādyāham antaram praviśāmi sukhasparśaṃ vinaśiṣyāmy asaṃśayam
english: If I do not enter today between the arms of that hero, so pleasant to the touch, I shall surely perish — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yadi māṃ meghanirghoṣo nopagacchati naiṣadhaḥ adya cāmīkaraprakhyo vinaśiṣyāmy asaṃśayam
english: If the Niṣadhan, whose voice is like thunder, golden in lustre, does not come to me today, I shall surely perish — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yadi māṃ siṃhavikrānto mattavāraṇavāraṇaḥ nābhigacchati rājendro vinaśiṣyāmy asaṃśayam
english: If the lord of kings, bold as a lion, matchless as a rutting elephant, does not come to me, I shall surely perish — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: na smarāmy anṛtaṃ kiṃ cin na smarāmy anupākṛtam na ca paryuṣitaṃ vākyaṃ svaireṣv api mahātmanaḥ
english: I do not recall any falsehood from him, nor any unkindness, nor even a stale word spoken carelessly by that great soul.

sanskrit: prabhuḥ kṣamāvān vīraś ca mṛdur dānto jitendriyaḥ raho 'nīcānuvartī ca klībavan mama naiṣadhaḥ
english: Master of himself, forbearing, heroic, gentle, self-controlled, with conquered senses, and in private never bowing to the base — my Niṣadhan was docile as a child.

sanskrit: guṇāṃs tasya smarantyā me tatparāyā divāniśam hṛdayaṃ dīryata idaṃ śokāt priyavinākṛtam
english: As I, devoted entirely to him, recall his virtues day and night, this heart of mine, bereft of my beloved, is riven by grief.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evaṃ vilapamānā sā naṣṭasaṃjñeva bhārata āruroha mahad veśma puṇyaślokadidṛkṣayā
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Thus lamenting, she, like one who had lost her senses, O Bhārata, ascended the great palace longing to behold the one of blessed renown.

sanskrit: tato madhyamakakṣāyāṃ dadarśa ratham āsthitam ṛtuparṇaṃ mahīpālaṃ sahavārṣṇeyabāhukam
english: Then in the middle courtyard she saw the chariot with Ṛtuparṇa, the guardian of the earth, standing in it together with Vārṣṇeya and Bāhuka.

sanskrit: tato 'vatīrya vārṣṇeyo bāhukaś ca rathottamāt hayāṃs tān avamucyātha sthāpayām āsatū ratham
english: Then Vārṣṇeya and Bāhuka alighted from that finest of chariots, unyoked those horses, and stationed the chariot.

sanskrit: so 'vatīrya rathopasthād ṛtuparṇo narādhipaḥ upatasthe mahārāja bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam
english: Alighting from the body of the chariot, Ṛtuparṇa, lord of men, presented himself, O great king, before Bhīma of terrible prowess.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaḥ pratijagrāha pūjayā parayā tataḥ akasmāt sahasā prāptaṃ strīmantraṃ na sma vindati
english: Bhīma received him with the highest honour; but the secret purpose concerning his daughter, for which he had come so suddenly and unexpectedly, Bhīma could not fathom.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ svāgataṃ te 'stu rājñā pṛṣṭaś ca bhārata nābhijajñe sa nṛpatir duhitrarthe samāgatam
english: "What is your business? Welcome" — so asked by the king, O Bhārata, that lord of men did not reveal that he had come on account of his daughter.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇo 'pi rājā sa dhīmān satyaparākramaḥ rājānaṃ rājaputraṃ vā na sma paśyati kaṃ cana naiva svayaṃvarakathāṃ na ca viprasamāgamam
english: King Ṛtuparṇa too, wise and of true valour, saw neither king nor prince present there, nor any sign of a svayaṃvara assembly, nor any gathering of brahmins.

sanskrit: tato vigaṇayan rājā manasā kosalādhipaḥ āgato 'smīty uvācainaṃ bhavantam abhivādakaḥ
english: Then the king, lord of Kosala, reflecting in his mind, said to him: "I have come to pay my respects to you."

sanskrit: rājāpi ca smayan bhīmo manasābhivicintayat adhikaṃ yojanaśataṃ tasyāgamanakāraṇam
english: King Bhīma too, smiling inwardly, pondered the reason for his journey of more than a hundred yojanas.

sanskrit: grāmān bahūn atikramya nādhyagacchad yathātatham alpakāryaṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ tasyāgamanakāraṇam
english: Passing over many villages, he had not found things as expected; the stated purpose of his coming seemed trivial indeed.

sanskrit: naitad evaṃ sa nṛpatis taṃ satkṛtya vyasarjayat viśrāmyatām iti vadan klānto 'sīti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Thus reasoning, that lord of men honoured him and dismissed him, saying again and again: "Rest — you must be weary."

sanskrit: sa satkṛtaḥ prahṛṣṭātmā prītaḥ prītena pārthivaḥ rājapreṣyair anugato diṣṭaṃ veśma samāviśat
english: Honoured and cheerful of heart, delighted by the delighted king, escorted by royal attendants, he entered the appointed dwelling.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇe gate rājan vārṣṇeyasahite nṛpe bāhuko ratham āsthāya rathaśālām upāgamat
english: After Ṛtuparṇa the king had departed, O king, along with Vārṣṇeya, Bāhuka led the chariot to the carriage-stable.

sanskrit: sa mocayitvā tān aśvān paricārya ca śāstrataḥ svayaṃ caitān samāśvāsya rathopastha upāviśat
english: Having unyoked those horses and tended to them according to the rules, he himself comforted them and then sat down in the body of the chariot.

sanskrit: damayantī tu śokārtā dṛṣṭvā bhāṅgasvariṃ nṛpam sūtaputraṃ ca vārṣṇeyaṃ bāhukaṃ ca tathāvidham
english: But Damayantī, stricken with grief, having seen the king Bhāṅgasvari, the charioteer's son Vārṣṇeya, and Bāhuka in such a guise —

sanskrit: cintayām āsa vaidarbhī kasyaiṣa rathanisvanaḥ nalasyeva mahān āsīn na ca paśyāmi naiṣadham
english: — the daughter of Vidarbha pondered: "Whose was this great chariot-sound, so like Nala's? Yet I do not see the Niṣadhan."

sanskrit: vārṣṇeyena bhaven nūnaṃ vidyā saivopaśikṣitā tenāsya rathanirghoṣo nalasyeva mahān abhūt
english: "Perhaps Vārṣṇeya learned that very skill from him — and therefore his chariot-roar has become as great as Nala's."

sanskrit: āho svid ṛtuparṇo 'pi yathā rājā nalas tathā tato 'yaṃ rathanirghoṣo naiṣadhasyeva lakṣyate
english: "Or could Ṛtuparṇa himself drive as king Nala does — and hence this chariot-roar is marked as like the Niṣadhan's?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vitarkayitvā tu damayantī viśāṃ pate dūtīṃ prasthāpayām āsa naiṣadhānveṣaṇe nṛpa
english: Having thus deliberated, Damayantī, O lord of the people, O king, sent a female messenger to search out the Niṣadhan.

sanskrit: damayanty uvāca gaccha keśini jānīhi ka eṣa rathavāhakaḥ upaviṣṭo rathopasthe vikṛto hrasvabāhukaḥ
english: Damayantī said: Go, Keśinī, find out who this charioteer is — disfigured, short-armed Bāhuka, seated in the body of the chariot.

sanskrit: abhyetya kuśalaṃ bhadre mṛdupūrvaṃ samāhitā pṛcchethāḥ puruṣaṃ hy enaṃ yathātattvam anindite
english: Approach him, dear one, and enquire after his well-being; then, composed, question this man gently and learn the truth about him, O blameless one.

sanskrit: atra me mahatī śaṅkā bhaved eṣa nalo nṛpaḥ tathā ca me manastuṣṭir hṛdayasya ca nirvṛtiḥ
english: I have a great suspicion about this: he may be king Nala — for so too does my mind feel satisfied and my heart find peace.

sanskrit: brūyāś cainaṃ kathānte tvaṃ parṇādavacanaṃ yathā prativākyaṃ ca suśroṇi budhyethās tvam anindite
english: At the end of the conversation you must tell him the words of Parṇāda exactly, O fair-hipped one, and then discern his reply, O blameless one.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evaṃ samāhitā gatvā dūtī bāhukam abravīt damayanty api kalyāṇī prāsādasthānvavaikṣata
english: Bṛhadaśva said: The messenger, thus composed, went and spoke to Bāhuka; and the auspicious Damayantī, standing on the terrace, watched on.

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca svāgataṃ te manuṣyendra kuśalaṃ te bravīmy aham damayantyā vacaḥ sādhu nibodha puruṣarṣabha
english: Keśinī said: Welcome to you, O lord among men; I convey your well-being from Damayantī — hear her words well, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kadā vai prasthitā yūyaṃ kimartham iha cāgatāḥ tat tvaṃ brūhi yathānyāyaṃ vaidarbhī śrotum icchati
english: When did you set out, and for what purpose have you come here? Tell me truthfully — the daughter of Vidarbha wishes to hear.

sanskrit: bāhuka uvāca śrutaḥ svayaṃvaro rājñā kausalyena yaśasvinā dvitīyo damayantyā vai śvobhūta iti bhāmini
english: Bāhuka said: The illustrious king of Kosala heard that a second svayaṃvara of Damayantī was to take place tomorrow, O fair lady.

sanskrit: śrutvā taṃ prasthito rājā śatayojanayāyibhiḥ hayair vātajavair mukhyair aham asya ca sārathiḥ
english: Hearing that, the king set out with horses swift as the wind that can cover a hundred yojanas, and I am his charioteer.

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca atha yo 'sau tṛtīyo vaḥ sa kutaḥ kasya vā punaḥ tvaṃ ca kasya kathaṃ cedaṃ tvayi karma samāhitam
english: Keśinī said: And this third person of yours — where does he come from, and to whom does he belong? And whose man are you, and how did this service come to be placed in you?

sanskrit: bāhuka uvāca puṇyaślokasya vai sūto vārṣṇeya iti viśrutaḥ sa nale vidrute bhadre bhāṅgasvarim upasthitaḥ
english: Bāhuka said: He is a charioteer of the blessed Nala, celebrated as Vārṣṇeya; when Nala fled, O dear one, he attached himself to Bhāṅgasvari.

sanskrit: aham apy aśvakuśalaḥ sūdatve ca suniṣṭhitaḥ ṛtuparṇena sārathye bhojane ca vṛtaḥ svayam
english: I myself am skilled with horses and well-established as a cook; Ṛtuparṇa himself took me on for the driving of chariots and for cooking.

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca atha jānāti vārṣṇeyaḥ kva nu rājā nalo gataḥ kathaṃ cit tvayi vaitena kathitaṃ syāt tu bāhuka
english: Keśinī said: Does Vārṣṇeya know where king Nala has gone? Has he perhaps told you anything about it, Bāhuka?

sanskrit: bāhuka uvāca ihaiva putrau nikṣipya nalasyāśubhakarmaṇaḥ gatas tato yathākāmaṃ naiṣa jānāti naiṣadham
english: Bāhuka said: Having left his two children here, after that evil act of Nala's, he went wherever he wished; he does not know where the Niṣadhan is.

sanskrit: na cānyaḥ puruṣaḥ kaś cin nalaṃ vetti yaśasvini gūḍhaś carati loke 'smin naṣṭarūpo mahīpatiḥ
english: Nor does any other man know Nala, O renowned lady; the king wanders in this world concealed, deprived of his own form.

sanskrit: ātmaiva hi nalaṃ vetti yā cāsya tadanantarā na hi vai tāni liṅgāni nalaṃ śaṃsanti karhi cit
english: Only Nala himself knows Nala — and the one who is closest to him next; for those outward marks never truly reveal Nala at any time.

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca yo 'sāv ayodhyāṃ prathamaṃ gatavān brāhmaṇas tadā imāni nārīvākyāni kathayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Keśinī said: That brahmin who went first to Ayodhyā at that time, reciting again and again these words of a woman —

sanskrit: kva nu tvaṃ kitava chittvā vastrārdhaṃ prasthito mama utsṛjya vipine suptām anuraktāṃ priyāṃ priya
english: "Where have you gone, O gambler, cutting off half my garment and setting out, abandoning your beloved who lay sleeping in the forest, devoted to you, O dear one?" —

sanskrit: sā vai yathā samādiṣṭā tatrāste tvatpratīkṣiṇī dahyamānā divārātraṃ vastrārdhenābhisaṃvṛtā
english: "She, as you instructed, abides there waiting for you, burning day and night, covered only by half a garment" —

sanskrit: tasyā rudantyāḥ satataṃ tena duḥkhena pārthiva prasādaṃ kuru vai vīra prativākyaṃ prayaccha ca
english: "Show grace, O hero, O king, to her who weeps constantly in that pain — give her an answer" —

sanskrit: tasyās tat priyam ākhyānaṃ prabravīhi mahāmate tad eva vākyaṃ vaidarbhī śrotum icchaty aninditā
english: Speak that dear story of hers, O great-minded one; that very word the blameless daughter of Vidarbha wishes to hear from you.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā prativacas tasya dattaṃ tvayā kila yat purā tat punas tvatto vaidarbhī śrotum icchati
english: The response you gave upon hearing that then — the daughter of Vidarbha wishes to hear that again from you.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca evam uktasya keśinyā nalasya kurunandana hṛdayaṃ vyathitaṃ cāsīd aśrupūrṇe ca locane
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Thus addressed by Keśinī, O joy of the Kurus, Nala's heart was afflicted and his eyes filled with tears.

sanskrit: sa nigṛhyātmano duḥkhaṃ dahyamāno mahīpatiḥ bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā vācā punar evedam abravīt
english: Suppressing his own grief, burning within, the lord of the earth spoke again with a voice choked with tears.

sanskrit: vaiṣamyam api saṃprāptā gopāyanti kulastriyaḥ ātmānam ātmanā satyo jitasvargā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Even when fallen into adversity, noble women guard themselves by themselves; true women of such virtue win heaven — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: rahitā bhartṛbhiś caiva na krudhyanti kadā cana prāṇāṃś cāritrakavacā dhārayantīha satstriyaḥ
english: Separated from their husbands, true women never grow angry at any time; they sustain their lives here clad in the armour of good conduct.

sanskrit: prāṇayātrāṃ pariprepsoḥ śakunair hṛtavāsasaḥ ādhibhir dahyamānasya śyāmā na kroddhum arhati
english: The dark-complexioned one ought not to be angry with one who was struggling to preserve his life, from whom birds had stolen his garment, and who was burning with anguish.

sanskrit: satkṛtāsatkṛtā vāpi patiṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatam bhraṣṭarājyaṃ śriyā hīnaṃ kṣudhitaṃ vyasanāplutam
english: Whether honoured or dishonoured, seeing a husband come in such a state — fallen from his kingdom, destitute of fortune, hungry, overwhelmed by calamity —

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇas tad vākyaṃ nalaḥ paramaduḥkhitaḥ na bāṣpam aśakat soḍhuṃ praruroda ca bhārata
english: Speaking these words thus, Nala, deeply tormented, could not hold back his tears and wept aloud, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā keśinī gatvā damayantyai nyavedayat tat sarvaṃ kathitaṃ caiva vikāraṃ caiva tasya tam
english: Then Keśinī went and reported to Damayantī all that had been said, and also that emotional change she had seen in him.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca damayantī tu tac chrutvā bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇā śaṅkamānā nalaṃ taṃ vai keśinīm idam abravīt
english: Bṛhadaśva said: But Damayantī, hearing that, deeply absorbed in grief, suspecting that he might indeed be Nala, said this to Keśinī.

sanskrit: gaccha keśini bhūyas tvaṃ parīkṣāṃ kuru bāhuke ābruvāṇā samīpasthā caritāny asya lakṣaya
english: Go again, Keśinī, and test Bāhuka; stand near him speaking to him, and observe his behaviour.

sanskrit: yadā ca kiṃ cit kuryāt sa kāraṇaṃ tatra bhāmini tatra saṃceṣṭamānasya saṃlakṣyaṃ te viceṣṭitam
english: And whenever he performs some action there, O fair lady, carefully mark his movements as he goes about.

sanskrit: na cāsya pratibandhena deyo 'gnir api bhāmini yācate na jalaṃ deyaṃ samyag atvaramāṇayā
english: Do not give him fire when he is obstructed either, O fair lady; and do not give water immediately when he asks — take your time properly.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ samīkṣya tvaṃ caritaṃ me nivedaya yac cānyad api paśyethās tac cākhyeyaṃ tvayā mama
english: Having observed all this, report his conduct to me; and whatever else you may see, that too you must tell me.

sanskrit: damayantyaivam uktā sā jagāmāthāśu keśinī niśāmya ca hayajñasya liṅgāni punar āgamat
english: Thus addressed by Damayantī, Keśinī went quickly and, having observed the marks of the horse-knower, returned.

sanskrit: sā tat sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ damayantyai nyavedayat nimittaṃ yat tadā dṛṣṭaṃ bāhuke divyamānuṣam
english: She reported to Damayantī everything exactly as it happened — the sign she had seen in Bāhuka that was both divine and human.

sanskrit: keśiny uvāca dṛḍhaṃ śucyupacāro 'sau na mayā mānuṣaḥ kva cit dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ śruto vāpi damayanti tathāvidhaḥ
english: Keśinī said: His manner of service is immaculate — never before have I seen or heard of a man like that, O Damayantī.

sanskrit: hrasvam āsādya saṃcāraṃ nāsau vinamate kva cit taṃ tu dṛṣṭvā yathāsaṅgam utsarpati yathāsukham saṃkaṭe 'py asya sumahad vivaraṃ jāyate 'dhikam
english: Approaching a low passage, he does not stoop anywhere; yet seeing it, he rises naturally as it suits him — even in a narrow space a very large opening is created for him.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇasya cārthāya bhojanīyam anekaśaḥ preṣitaṃ tatra rājñā ca māṃsaṃ subahu pāśavam
english: For Ṛtuparṇa's meal, food was sent in many portions by the king, and a large quantity of animal meat as well.

sanskrit: tasya prakṣālanārthāya kumbhas tatropakalpitaḥ sa tenāvekṣitaḥ kumbhaḥ pūrṇa evābhavat tadā
english: A water-pot was prepared there for washing it; he merely glanced at that pot and it became full straightaway.
